subject: pcountOpen not incorporating dynamics (survival and recruitment)

messages.author: f0c4c757f6cbcd73
messages.subject: pcountOpen not incorporating dynamics (survival and recruitment)
parts:
Hi all,
        I'm trying to estimate the number of kits or offspring corrected by detectability. I have sampled many sites for three years and I have secondary sampling periods. My main goal is to estimate the mean number of kits or offspring as a way to calculate "effective fecundity". Of course, survival and recruitment are not of interest, because each year I'm looking at the newborns. Is still valid to use the Dail Madsen model where the main focus is to estimate N through S and G?.
Should I use the "trend"dynamics where survival and recruitment are not the parameters of interest, or alternatively should I fit open models in winBUGS as suggested by Kery 2009 or others?

Thanks for your input!

Alejandro

messages.author: 0e6ec3cbd3336f19
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcountOpen not incorporating dynamics (survival and recruitment)
parts:
Hi Alejandro,

I think the answer to your question depends on the biology of the species and your sampling methods, but you might be able to fit N-mixture models to each year independently. Or, you might be able to use a model that Elise Zipkin just developed, which extends the Dail-Madsen model to stage-structured populations. The model requires that have counts of both adults and kits. Elise, can you send Alejandro the manuscript? 

Richard
